The rain drummed a relentless, hollow rhythm against the windowpane of the cramped apartment, but Elias didn’t hear it. He was focused entirely on the ritual.

His hands, usually prone to a fine, nervous tremor, were steady now. He moved with the practiced, mechanical efficiency of someone performing a task they had done a thousand times before. The small, crinkled baggie sat on the scarred wooden table like a coiled snake. 

He didn't think about the "why" anymore. The "why" was a ghost that had long since been exorcised by the "how." The "how" was the only thing that kept the world from splintering into jagged, unbearable edges.

He prepared the dose, his movements fluid and detached. The room smelled of stale coffee and the metallic tang of the radiator. When he finally leaned back against the peeling wallpaper, the transition was instantaneous.
